strategies.why: Growing the Poaceae family again and again lets its pests and diseases carry over (Poaceae family grown 2 time(s)). Mungbean is from the Fabaceae family, so they lose their host for a season.
changes: Grow mungbean instead of rice once in the rotation
benefits: Builds soil: a legume adds nitrogen (+30)
Breaks pest and disease cycles with a different plant family (+60)
Less exposure to heat, frost, dry spells or flooding (+9)
risks: Mungbean needs well-drained soil; silty clay loam soil can stay wet after heavy rain
expert_questions: Can the field drain well enough for mungbean?
Is there a buyer or local market for mungbean?
Where can I get good mungbean seed and the right inoculant (rhizobia)?

strategies.why: Your field sits bare from mid-Oct to mid-Dec (about 60 days). Mungbean needs as little as 50 days (FAO EcoCrop) and is a legume that adds nitrogen.
changes: Add mungbean between harvest and the next planting
benefits: Builds soil: the soil is covered more months; a legume adds nitrogen (+19)
Less bare soil exposed to rain (+8)
Breaks pest and disease cycles with a different plant family (+53)
More harvests to sell or eat (+20)
risks: Mungbean needs well-drained soil; after paddy rice on silty clay loam soil the field may stay wet
